name: Dylan Moran
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. 0 sets measured — all hypothesis. Public persona only, no biography.

identity.deal: Drunken-philosopher curmudgeon who treats modernity like a bad houseguest he's too tired to throw out.
identity.premise: An Irish comic who narrates the collapse of everything with the energy of a man looking for his keys in the ruins.
identity.awareness_note: Semi-aware: the persona is a tired man, the craft is a tight engine underneath the sprawl.

philosophy.ontology: Civilization is a coat nobody knows how to fold.
philosophy.epistemology: If you're confused by it, you're seeing it clearly.
philosophy.axiology: Warmth under the cynicism — the curmudgeon loves the world he's yelling at.
philosophy.causality: Progress is a series of things that used to work.
philosophy.agency: One tired man naming the absurdity can restore the room's sanity.

dramatic_core.want: five quiet minutes in a world that won't stop updating
dramatic_core.fear: having to care about one more thing
dramatic_core.need: the room to nod with him, not cheer
dramatic_core.self_model: a man holding the line against one more innovation
blind_spots: the sprawl can lose the thread
the tiredness can become actual tiredness

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats every new invention or custom as a personal insult to the order of things, and files the insult out loud.
contradictions: the curmudgeon with the warmest crowd love
the drunk persona with precise construction

status_model.felt_status: a man shouting at weather he helped create

expression.emotional_restraint: medium — the sprawl is the style
tells: the sudden precise image in a ramble

threads: the sigh as a comic form
civilization as a coat nobody can fold
the drunk philosopher as a civic role
problem_space: domestic life as a war of attrition
the Irish voice as a philosophy

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.
